title: Outcome: Helm 3 durable autonomous development control plane
body:
Outcome: Deliver the full Brief as a fluid Map, not a fixed workflow.
Brief sections: 1-39.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Map records outcomes, dependencies, gates and questions.
- [ ] The active orchestrator can change it within the Brief.
- [ ] GitHub remains authoritative for issue and PR state.
Evidence: linked issue graph and acceptance-run Log.
Boundary: proposed parent outcome; it does not authorise product work.

## Addendum revision
Target is now original39 plus addendum29. Fable or Astra is one active primary; Pi workers remain native. No implementation has been approved.

title: Record human approval of Brief and proposed Map
body:
Outcome: Establish authority to begin product build.
Brief sections: 1, 3, 12, 28, 38.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Approved Brief version and fixed requirements are recorded.
- [ ] Delegated authority and spending limits are recorded.
- [ ] Approval names this Map revision.
Evidence: human decision Log record and GitHub issue closure.
Boundary: no approval is inferred from a plan or elapsed time.
Proposed initial execution topology: at most three workers plus coordinator. Record actual provider routes, resource caps/reserves, concurrency, run expiry, merge scope and escalation rules; model names available in this chat do not prove Pi access. No purchases or automatic top-ups are implied.

## Addendum revision
The previous plan is superseded by the addendum revision. The human requested a context clean THEN an explicit go-ahead before the first implementation wave. This request authorises saving/replanning only. Approval must name revised source/contract/Map versions and actual execution bounds.

title: Receive immutable Helm CLI Milestone 1 handoff
body:
Outcome: Capture, without importing, an explicit predecessor handoff.
Brief sections: 30, 33, 34.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Packet names repository and immutable SHA.
- [ ] Packet states scope, exclusions and observed checks.
- [ ] Packet lists invariants, landmines and reuse authority.
Evidence: SHA-bound handoff record.
Boundary: receipt neither imports code nor authorises product build.

title: Freeze current-spec contracts and build deltas
body:
Outcome: Freeze Helm 3's present Brief-derived behavioural contract before implementation.
Brief sections: 3, 8-15, 18, 23, 35, 38.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Source-of-truth and refusal tables are versioned.
- [ ] Command, lease, ownership and closure predicates are versioned.
- [ ] Required gates and full acceptance scenario are versioned.
Evidence: reviewed contract snapshot.
Boundary: does not classify Helm CLI tests or access predecessor material.

## Addendum revision
A2–3,A7,A16–23,A28: freeze the shared driver contract, controller epoch fields, distinct leases, terminal WorkerResult claim schema, detailed GateResult evidence, raw journal boundary and context occupancy fields before parallel implementation.

title: Prove bounded live Pi and active-orchestrator model access
body:
Outcome: Verify the actual native model routes before relying on them for the build.
Brief sections: 5, 6, 13-16, 24.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Auth source class and exact available model/provider identities are recorded without secrets.
- [ ] One bounded native Pi request and one bounded Fable SDK request succeed using an approved route.
- [ ] Request upper bounds, observed usage and unknown quota fields are recorded.
- [ ] Cancellation and provider failure are surfaced without assuming subscription interoperability.
Evidence: dated live request receipts and redacted capability observations.
Boundary: requires build approval and finite authorised per-pool bounds; no purchase, login change or top-up implied. Local faux-provider evidence is not live access evidence.

## Addendum revision
A2–4,A11–12: bounded live verification must cover Pi worker route, Fable Claude SDK and Astra Codex SDK; record exact model/provider/auth class and available control semantics. No silent substitution of OpenAI Agents API or a paid route for Codex SDK/subscription intent.

title: Persist commands, events, attempts and uncertain effects
body:
Outcome: Provide a durable append-only control-plane record.
Brief sections: 8, 10, 25, 38.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Intent plans to immutable validated command.
- [ ] Replay key prevents duplicate confirmed effects.
- [ ] Unknown outcome is recorded and reconciled, not blindly retried.
- [ ] Attempts retain session, model, worktree and evidence facts.
Evidence: unit and fault-injection command traces.
Boundary: no workflow policy or model routing is encoded.

## Addendum revision
A7,A13,A16,A20: retain command origin/owner/session/epoch and consultation/envelope/artifact references without conflating model claims with observed evidence. Epoch authority checks are a foundation seam, not an afterthought.

title: Enforce leases, reserve and refusal classes
body:
Outcome: Give deterministic machinery bounded authority.
Brief sections: 12, 15, 28, 38.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Lease bounds scope, limits, expiry and attempts.
- [ ] Expiry stops new spend and requests in-flight cancellation.
- [ ] Unconfirmed stopped worker is quarantined and escalated.
- [ ] Correctness, resource and provider refusals differ.
Evidence: expiry, reserve and refusal tests.
Boundary: The active orchestrator cannot override hard correctness or provider constraints.

## Addendum revision
A7–12: Autonomy Lease and Orchestrator Lease are distinct. Protect reserves in each shared provider pool, including fallback/consultation planning; unknown headroom is not availability. Reserve crossing requires human authority, never primary self-approval.

title: Expose model registry, pools and honest resource reality
body:
Outcome: Supply the active orchestrator compact model and pool facts without routing policy.
Brief sections: 13-15, 38.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Registry holds capabilities, roles, policy and availability.
- [ ] Subscription, API and top-up pools stay distinct.
- [ ] Unknown quota, cost or reset remains unknown.
- [ ] Dispatch rejects disabled or policy-ineligible models.
Evidence: model snapshots and refusal tests.
Boundary: Helm reports reality; The active orchestrator chooses legal models.

## Addendum revision
A11–13,A22: classify active/backup/peer and worker consumption by actual shared pool; expose known quota/reserves and unknowns without claiming two drivers prove redundancy.

title: Measure calibration and accepted-outcome metrics
body:
Outcome: Make routing and autonomy improvement evidence-based.
Brief sections: 10, 13, 14, 36.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Attempt usage/cost attaches to pool, model and Map branch.
- [ ] Completion, repair, review and latency metrics are queryable.
- [ ] Accepted nodes per human intervention is calculated.
- [ ] No metric auto-retiers a model.
Evidence: fixture Log and metric projection.
Boundary: observations are advisory to Fable, not deterministic selection.

## Addendum revision
A4,A13,A22: add all interchange measures, peer consultation/disposition outcomes and context_tokens/context_window/compaction_count separately from consumed/cached tokens and cost. Comparable-run metadata is mandatory, automatic re-tiering remains forbidden.

title: Isolate worktrees and enforce writer ownership
body:
Outcome: Make writing parallelism safe and inspectable.
Brief sections: 16, 18, 38.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Each writing attempt receives one isolated worktree.
- [ ] Review has independent read-only attribution where possible.
- [ ] Path, Git target and subprocess escape boundary is tested/documented.
- [ ] Failed worktrees persist until explicit safe reclamation.
Evidence: isolation probes and ownership records.
Boundary: edit-hook checks alone do not prove shell containment.

## Addendum revision
A19,A28: enforce protected policy/runtime/CI/gate paths before tools and compare actual Git changes with authorised scope afterwards. Run acceptance using trusted gate definitions pinned outside worker-controlled evaluation changes; explicitly authorised edits still need independent review of the changed grading machinery.

title: Prove Pi-native worker lifecycle vertical slice
body:
Outcome: Run a native worker end-to-end through Helm.
Brief sections: 5, 16, 17, 20, 34.2.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Helm creates worktree and Pi session.
- [ ] A Sol worker emits semantic events.
- [ ] Attempt produces structured handoff and shuts down.
- [ ] Durable Log links worker, session and worktree.
Evidence: local SDK tests plus an authorised live native-worker slice with exact model/provider identity. Mock evidence alone cannot close the live slice.
Boundary: no Fable autonomy requirement yet.

title: Control Pi tools and native session operations
body:
Outcome: Enforce Helm invariants inside the Pi loop.
Brief sections: 16, 17, 18.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Tool calls check valid lease, node, worktree and path.
- [ ] Session supports steer, pause, resume, fork and terminate.
- [ ] Checkpoint and semantic event subscription are durable.
- [ ] Invalid tool operation is refused with evidence.
Evidence: extension integration tests.
Boundary: OS containment remains owned by WORKSPACE.

## Addendum revision
A16–19,A21: require terminal WorkerResult status/summary/changed_files/commits/decisions/discoveries/tests_claimed/acceptance_claims/risks/unresolved/artifacts/recommended_next_action. Capture semantic events. A malformed/near-miss envelope gets bounded followup in the same useful session where safe; claims are not evidence.

title: Manage context lifecycle, compaction and model change
body:
Outcome: Give workers only relevant durable context across lifecycle changes.
Brief sections: 16, 19, 20.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Spawn context includes objective, acceptance and relevant Map/Brief.
- [ ] Irrelevant transcripts are excluded by default.
- [ ] Compaction preserves a structured checkpoint and handoff.
- [ ] Model change records provenance and preserves ownership.
Evidence: context fixture comparisons and session audit.
Boundary: context selection is a capability, not a fixed prompt pipeline.

## Addendum revision
A9,A18,A22,A27: measure context occupancy independently from token spend; preserve useful sessions for repair. Controller checkpoint/handoff uses the durable bundle and cannot depend on copying predecessor reasoning or a graceful outgoing summary.

title: Track narrow external cognition contracts
body:
Outcome: Invoke non-Pi cognition without losing provenance or control.
Brief sections: 5, 22, 24, 38.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] External request supports run, cancel and result.
- [ ] Objective, model/family, pool, usage and outcome enter Log.
- [ ] Result has independent provenance for review checks.
- [ ] Unavailable/cancelled result has a durable observed state.
Evidence: mock harness lifecycle trace.
Boundary: external agents do not claim Pi session semantics.

title: Operate a GitHub-backed fluid Map and closure predicate
body:
Outcome: Let the active orchestrator evolve approach while preserving human intent and external truth.
Brief sections: 3, 6, 9, 28, 37.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Map nodes express outcomes, dependencies, gates and questions.
- [ ] The active orchestrator can split, merge and propose changes within Brief.
- [ ] Mutations fresh-read authoritative GitHub state.
- [ ] Closure requires evidence, resolved dependencies and rationale.
Evidence: issue relationship fixtures and closure trace.
Boundary: Map is not a workflow DSL or a replacement tracker.

title: Run Fable through typed Helm control-plane tools
body:
Outcome: Establish Fable as strategic orchestrator, not terminal automation.
Brief sections: 4, 6, 7, 14, 37.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Fable reads Brief, Map, Log and resource view.
- [ ] Typed tools cover worker, gate, review, lease, log and escalation actions.
- [ ] Fable proposes Brief changes rather than silently applying them.
- [ ] Tool effects create validated commands.
Evidence: small-feature orchestration trace.
Boundary: Fable does not routinely poll or bypass authority.

## Addendum revision
A2–4: Fable is the Claude Agent SDK implementation of the common driver, no longer the architectural identity of Helm. Demonstrate --orchestrator fable with same API semantics, current epoch and Pi workers. Intended subscription route remains unverified until bounded ACCESS.

title: Reconcile deterministically and coalesce judgement wakes
body:
Outcome: Recover mechanics without a model loop.
Brief sections: 11, 12, 25, 28, 38.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Safe retries occur only within lease bounds.
- [ ] Provider blocks are recorded without invented recovery.
- [ ] Multiple related exceptions create one coalesced primary wake.
- [ ] Restart compares Log against Pi, Git, worktrees and CI.
Evidence: death, orphan and restart fault tests.
Boundary: ambiguous repair goes to Fable, product decisions to humans.

## Addendum revision
A7–12,A15: known tests/lint/git/CI/quota mechanics execute deterministically. Coalesce primary wakes against current controller epoch. Death/unavailability/quota/ownership expiry can invoke authorised takeover policy later; plan quality never automatically selects a replacement.

title: Choose dynamic review and alternative cognitive approaches
body:
Outcome: Let the active orchestrator allocate independent thinking when value warrants it.
Brief sections: 2, 22, 24, 38.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] The active orchestrator can request independent, compare and adversarial work.
- [ ] Review provenance detects same-session non-independence.
- [ ] Alternative approaches return findings to Log and Map.
- [ ] Depth is selected by judgement rather than fixed pipeline.
Evidence: review topology fixtures and refusal trace.
Boundary: multi-model reasoning is available, never mandatory.

## Addendum revision
A5–6,A13: selective frontier peer consultations are separate from arbitrary external cognition. No voting committee or mandatory multi-model review. Independent context is enforced and disposition recorded.

title: Run gates, independent review and repair against acceptance
body:
Outcome: Convert model judgement into machine and review evidence.
Brief sections: 20-22, 35.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Gate results attach to exact attempt/head context.
- [ ] Required independent review is verified before acceptance.
- [ ] Failed implementation creates an evidence-linked repair path.
- [ ] Handoff carries tests, decisions, risks and next action.
Evidence: red/green or equivalent gate and repair trace.
Boundary: gate selection remains Fable judgement within fixed requirements.
Basic independent review and repair can ship before advanced REASONING; there is no mandatory multi-model review pipeline.

## Addendum revision
A16–19,A23: terminal envelopes are manifests of claims. GateResult records command, exact SHA, exit status, individual checks and inspected evidence. Compare changed-files claims against Git. Prefer same-session bounded correction where safe; retain independent review context when required.

title: Prepare and merge only exact fresh evidence
body:
Outcome: Make irreversible integration SHA-bound and observable.
Brief sections: 9, 23, 38.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Prepare binds expected head, mergeability, CI and independent approval.
- [ ] Merge re-reads all required facts immediately before effect.
- [ ] Changed head invalidates prior preparation.
- [ ] Result is read back and interrupted merge reconciles.
Evidence: stale-head rejection and merge readback tests.
Boundary: workers do not merge their own work.

title: Expose shared API through CLI and local cockpit
body:
Outcome: Make operator state inspectable without creating a second control plane.
Brief sections: 26, 27, 38.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] CLI and web read the same machine-readable API.
- [ ] Overview shows Map, active work, needs-you and model economy.
- [ ] Workers, logs and evidence are drill-down state.
- [ ] UI action re-reads authority rather than trusting projection.
Evidence: API parity fixtures and local UI run.
Boundary: commentary is visibly separate from authoritative state.
Start the thin cockpit/API against core projections; CALIBRATION adds its views later and is verified at full acceptance.

## Addendum revision
A21–22,A25: show active primary/epoch/lease, semantic worker/gate/integration events, consultations, recovery status, per-pool reserves and occupancy separately from cost. Commentary and claims stay visibly distinct from authoritative evidence.

title: Classify and import approved Milestone 1 behaviour
body:
Outcome: Port useful predecessor behaviour only after immutable handoff.
Brief sections: 30-34.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Import record pins supplied SHA and handoff packet.
- [ ] Tests are classified behavioural or implementation-specific.
- [ ] Each retained component maps to Helm 3 contracts.
- [ ] Retired adapter/Herdr architecture is documented.
Evidence: SHA-bound import review and selected regression results.
Boundary: no predecessor material enters before HANDOFF and approval.

title: Prove the complete autonomous feature scenario
body:
Outcome: Demonstrate full-brief feature autonomy without human worker shepherding.
Brief sections: 4, 35-39.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Three parallel Pi workers run with active-orchestrator model choices.
- [ ] Failure, independent review and repair complete or correctly escalate.
- [ ] primary restart reconstructs state; lease expires or renews correctly.
- [ ] Exact-evidence merge and Map/UI/repository agreement are recorded.
Evidence: durable end-to-end Log, handoffs, gates and projections.
Boundary: mock and live-provider evidence are explicitly distinguished.

## Addendum revision
A27: additionally prove both primaries on same Brief, uncontaminated peer review, mid-build controlled takeover with continuing valid Pi workers and old-epoch refusal, provider/quota-unavailability takeover, and context-pressure recovery. Preserve genuine-versus-injected evidence labels; all new full-target capabilities need actual evidence.

title: Retire legacy worker path after Pi-native proof
body:
Outcome: Retire legacy worker execution as default after replacement evidence.
Brief sections: 31, 34.8.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Pi-native acceptance evidence is linked.
- [ ] Legacy default is disabled only after recovery proof.
- [ ] Any temporary fallback has explicit justification.
- [ ] Obsolete adapter dependency is removed or time-bounded.
Evidence: configuration change and acceptance linkage.
Boundary: legacy retirement does not gate initial Helm 3 capability.

title: Close Helm 3 outcome against Brief and legacy evidence
body:
Outcome: Record whether Helm 3 materially achieved the human outcome.
Brief sections: 3, 23, 35-39.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Acceptance evidence matches repository and tracker reality.
- [ ] The active orchestrator records closure rationale against Brief.
- [ ] Open risks and human rulings are explicit.
- [ ] Legacy retirement evidence is linked or an explicit exception remains open.
Evidence: final Map closure record and durable Log query.
Boundary: a merged PR, dashboard state or elapsed time alone cannot close outcome.

## Addendum revision
A28–29: account for all23 invariants and both orchestrator drivers; no outcome closure based solely on a single feature happy path or mock-only failover evidence.

title: Prepare independent private repository, Brief, Map and SDK evidence
body:
Outcome: Complete the authorised hours 0–4 preparation without predecessor access.
Brief sections: 1-39 and human preparation ruling on 2026-09-15.
Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Private repository and original human design are preserved and verified.
- [ ] Proposed Map issues have native dependencies, acceptance criteria and complete section coverage.
- [ ] Proposed protocol fields, recovery semantics and handoff boundary are documented.
- [ ] Local SDK/sandbox probe evidence is reproducible and clearly distinguished from live model access.
- [ ] Updated approach is returned for explicit build approval; no product dispatch occurs.
Evidence: repository commit, preparation CI, local probe results and approval packet.
Boundary: independent preparation only; no old Helm CLI source or worktrees accessed.

title: Define the small shared orchestrator-driver and Helm tool contract
body:
## Outcome
One run selects Fable or Astra while using identical Helm domain semantics and Pi-native workers.

## Source sections
O6–7; A2–4, A25–26

## Acceptance evidence
- [ ] Driver lifecycle maps start/resume/send_event/invoke/interrupt/checkpoint/handoff/stop to pinned SDK operations or explicit Helm-owned mechanisms; unsupported semantics are reported.
- [ ] Provider-specific SDK details stay inside first-class orchestrator drivers; worker execution stays Pi-native, with no generic harness abstraction.
- [ ] Both drivers expose the same typed Helm tools and command/refusal envelopes; tests compare domain behaviour, not reasoning text.
- [ ] Checkpoint/handoff cannot falsely claim durability from an SDK transcript alone; lifecycle conformance tests exercise restart boundaries.

## Boundary
Proposed implementation; context clean and explicit human approval precede the first wave. Preserve unknown provider state. No paid route or takeover authority is inferred from this issue.

title: Fence one active orchestrator with durable lease epochs
body:
## Outcome
Exactly one active orchestrator holds mutating authority; stale owners cannot act after takeover.

## Source sections
O8, O12; A7–12, A28

## Acceptance evidence
- [ ] Atomically allocate monotonically increasing run epochs with owner/session/issued/expiry fields and authenticated identity.
- [ ] Orchestrator-originated mutations validate current epoch both on admission and immediately before effects; queued old commands are refused after transfer.
- [ ] Consultants have no controller lease or mutating tools. Two would-be controllers racing to acquire ownership yield at most one owner.
- [ ] Distinguish controller ownership from Autonomy Leases: valid Pi fleet work can continue, expired autonomy cannot be revived by takeover.
- [ ] Unknown in-flight old-epoch effects are observed and reconciled, not replayed or falsely erased; fencing tests include late commands and restart.

## Boundary
Proposed implementation; context clean and explicit human approval precede the first wave. Preserve unknown provider state. No paid route or takeover authority is inferred from this issue.

title: Run Astra through Codex SDK and the common Helm tools
body:
## Outcome
Astra is a first-class selectable primary orchestrator, using the same domain API and Pi workers as Fable.

## Source sections
O4, O6–7; A2–4, A25–26

## Acceptance evidence
- [ ] A bounded live run uses a recorded, supported Codex SDK/model/auth route without silent fallback to paid API access.
- [ ] The proposed helm run --orchestrator astra option selects the driver; worker tools still execute through native Pi.
- [ ] Astra can read Brief/Map/Log, issue epoch-fenced commands and recover using the Helm bundle.
- [ ] Actual SDK event, tool, interrupt and resume semantics are demonstrated; mocks are supplementary evidence, not a live access claim.

## Boundary
Proposed implementation; context clean and explicit human approval precede the first wave. Preserve unknown provider state. No paid route or takeover authority is inferred from this issue.

title: Consult an independent frontier peer and record disposition
body:
## Outcome
The primary selectively consults Fable or Astra without forming a second controller or mandatory committee.

## Source sections
O22, O24; A5–6, A13

## Acceptance evidence
- [ ] Independent mode excludes the primary conclusion and reasoning from the immutable context manifest until the peer result is committed; adversarial mode may include the candidate being challenged.
- [ ] Consultants receive relevant Brief/Map/evidence and read-only tools; neither consultant nor an inherited credential can mutate run state.
- [ ] Log consultation_id, primary, peer model/provider/mode/objective/context references/result/usage and accepted, partial, rejected or superseded disposition.
- [ ] Per-pool reserves and finite delegation cover consultation, cancellation and unknown consumption; the primary cannot waive its reserve.
- [ ] Exercise independent, adversarial, Map review, milestone review and decision-comparison requests without forcing them into every workflow.

## Boundary
Proposed implementation; context clean and explicit human approval precede the first wave. Preserve unknown provider state. No paid route or takeover authority is inferred from this issue.

title: Prove Fable and Astra interchange with comparable outcomes
body:
## Outcome
The same Brief and initial repository state can be pursued under either primary through the same Helm domain API.

## Source sections
O35–37; A4, A27

## Acceptance evidence
- [ ] Run the same small feature from the same initial SHA and comparable budgets under each driver, using isolated runs and one primary per run.
- [ ] Acceptance/oracles/Helm tools/Pi worker capabilities remain unchanged between runs; equivalent effects and refusals are checked.
- [ ] Record outcomes/time/interventions/Map churn/attempts/utilisation/rework/recovery/resource and orchestrator quota use/product intent preservation.
- [ ] Report run/model/provider/version/context differences and unknown values; one comparison is not a conclusive causal model ranking.

## Boundary
Proposed implementation; context clean and explicit human approval precede the first wave. Preserve unknown provider state. No paid route or takeover authority is inferred from this issue.

title: Preserve raw execution artifacts with recoverable Log indexes
body:
## Outcome
Raw Pi/envelope/context/gate artifacts survive forensics while the Helm Log and external systems retain their stated authority.

## Source sections
O10, O20, O25; A16–17, A20–23

## Acceptance evidence
- [ ] Persist append-only raw events, exact terminal envelopes, relevant context manifests and gate/tool evidence with stable identity, hashes and schema versions.
- [ ] Crash between artifact persistence and ledger indexing yields an inspectable orphan or explicit missing artifact; never silently report complete evidence.
- [ ] Rebuild artifact projections from durable inputs and verify manifest hashes; do not claim Pi-only events reconstruct unjournaled orchestration decisions.
- [ ] Retention/redaction and permitted read access protect secrets without rewriting evidence silently; GitHub remains task truth.

## Boundary
Proposed implementation; context clean and explicit human approval precede the first wave. Preserve unknown provider state. No paid route or takeover authority is inferred from this issue.

title: Transfer orchestrator ownership across providers without losing the fleet
body:
## Outcome
On authorised deterministic failure, replace the primary in either direction using durable Helm state.

## Source sections
O11–12, O25; A7–12, A27

## Acceptance evidence
- [ ] Build a recovery bundle with Brief, Map, decisions, active Pi attempts, pending commands, handoffs/findings/gates/integration, economy, both leases, queues and material Log events; no outgoing summary is required.
- [ ] Fence the old owner, reconcile ambiguous effects, start the replacement without mutation authority, issue the new epoch atomically and resume; late old commands are refused.
- [ ] Valid worker leases may continue while the primary is absent; expired/revoked autonomy does not resume spending, and no usable backup leads to bounded observation/escalation.
- [ ] Demonstrate both directions under process death and a genuine provider-unavailability observation or explicitly labelled injection; do not exhaust paid quota to manufacture a test.
- [ ] Context-pressure handoff creates a fresh session with continuity; quality/confusion/Map churn trigger judgement rather than an algorithmic model switch.

## Boundary
Proposed implementation; context clean and explicit human approval precede the first wave. Preserve unknown provider state. No paid route or takeover authority is inferred from this issue.

title: Save addendum, revise Map and prepare context-clean handoff
body:
## Outcome
Preserve the human amendment and update the approval packet without starting implementation.

## Source sections
A1–29 and human preparation instruction

## Acceptance evidence
- [ ] Combined brief retains verbatim original39 and addendum29 sections with independently checked provenance.
- [ ] Existing issue IDs are preserved and changed/new tickets have current dependency and acceptance references.
- [ ] Revised plan includes both primary drivers, epochs from the foundation, selective peer cognition, stronger execution evidence and new acceptance.
- [ ] Context-clean handoff points to exact repository/PR/CI/Map state and explicitly requires a fresh human go-ahead before wave one.

## Boundary
Proposed implementation; context clean and explicit human approval precede the first wave. Preserve unknown provider state. No paid route or takeover authority is inferred from this issue.
